newsitem.title: UK: Britain's SFO probes CWS-Hobson contract.
newsitem.headline: Britain's SFO probes CWS-Hobson contract.

text.p: Britain's Serious Fraud Office (SFO) said on Tuesday it had started an investigation into a contract agreed in January 1995 between the Co-Operative Wholesale Society (CWS) and the Hobson Group, whose chief executive was thwarted last week in his attempt to take over the CWS.

Andrew Regan was head of Hobson when in 1994, it bought the CWS food manufacturing group. A supply agreement between the two was extended in January 1995, after negotiations between Regan and two CWS managers, who were dismissed over the weekend for their role in Regan's takeover attempt.

Regan, the 31-year-old behind the discredited 1.2 billion pound ($1.9 billion) takeover plan, has been incommunicado since his Guernsey-based investment trust Lanica and its offshoot Galileo admitted defeat in the face of CWS legal action and the withdrawal of a key backer.

The takeover was scotched last week by a High Court injunction granted to the CWS preventing the use of confidential information leaked to Regan, his business associate David Lyons and Lanica and Galileo.

Allan Green, the senior CWS executive who has admitted to passing on the highly sensitive papers, was sacked at the weekend following his suspension a week earlier. David Chambers, another CWS manager, was also sacked. The men negotiated with Regan the extension of Hobson's supply agreement with CWS in 1995.

During the course of its bid defence, CWS raised doubts about a 2.4 million pound payment to a third party called Trellis International. Regan has stated the money was paid by Hobson to Ronald Zimet at Trellis for "assisting with and conducting negotiations with CWS".
But the CWS was not happy with the answers it received from Regan and last week it passed on its concerns to the SFO which decided on Monday to open the probe.
SFO spokesman James O'Donoghue said the SFO was working in its investigation with the Greater Manchester police and the Metropolitan Police Fraud Squad.
